title: Pulling back from the point
statement:
Let $*_{\mathrm{proét}}$ be the pro-étale site of a point: profinite sets with
the coherent topology ([sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]). For a scheme $X$ let
$X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ be its small pro-étale site ([def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]),
and let $\pi_X\colon X\to\Spec\Z$ be the structure morphism. Since $\Spec\Z$ is
terminal, $\pi_Y\circ f=\pi_X$ for every morphism $f\colon X\to Y$.

1. **Profinite sets as pro-étale schemes.** For a profinite set $S$, let
   $LC(S,\Z)$ be the ring of locally constant functions $S\to\Z$. If $S_i$ runs
   over the finite quotients of $S$, then
   $$
   \Spec LC(S,\Z)=\lim_i\coprod_{S_i}\Spec\Z .
   $$
   The morphism $\Spec LC(S,\Z)\to\Spec\Z$ is weakly étale. Precomposition
   makes $S\mapsto\Spec LC(S,\Z)$ a functor
   $$
   u\colon *_{\mathrm{proét}}\longrightarrow(\Spec\Z)_{\mathrm{proét}} .
   $$
   It preserves finite limits, it sends finite jointly surjective families to
   pro-étale coverings, and it is continuous.

2. **Test objects.** For a scheme $X$ and a profinite set $S$, put
   $$
   X[S]:=\Spec LC(S,\Z)\times_{\Spec\Z}X=\lim_i\coprod_{S_i}X .
   $$
   The functor $u_X\colon *_{\mathrm{proét}}\to X_{\mathrm{proét}}$,
   $S\mapsto X[S]$, is $u$ followed by base change along $\pi_X$.

3. **Inverse image from the point.** Let
   $p_*\colon\Sh((\Spec\Z)_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)\to\Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$,
   $(p_*G)(S)=G(\Spec LC(S,\Z))$, be restriction along $u$. Define
   $$
   p^*:=\mathrm{sheafify}\circ\operatorname{Lan}_{u^{\mathrm{op}}}\colon
   \Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)\longrightarrow\Sh((\Spec\Z)_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab).
   $$
   Then $p^*$ is left adjoint to $p_*$. For the tensor products of
   [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], $p^*$ is strong monoidal and braided.

4. **Inverse image to $X$.** Define
   $$
   p_X^*:=\pi_X^*\circ p^*\colon
   \Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)\longrightarrow\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab),
   $$
   where $\pi_X^*$ is the pullback of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star]
   for $\mathcal A=\Ab$. It is strong monoidal and braided. It is a left
   adjoint, with right adjoint $G\mapsto\bigl(S\mapsto G(X[S])\bigr)$; so
   $p_X^*$ is the inverse image along $u_X$.

proof.text: The structure morphisms are unique: on each affine open of a scheme the unital ring map from $\Z$ is $n\mapsto n\cdot1$, and these maps agree on overlaps. Thus $\pi_Y\circ f=\pi_X$. By [lem-sfb-lc-weakly-etale], the morphism $\Spec LC(S,\Z)\to\Spec\Z$ is weakly étale, so it is an object of the small pro-étale site. Use the functor of [def-sfb-profinite-to-proetale]: for $g\colon S'\to S$, the corresponding ring map is $h\mapsto h\circ g$. This formula respects identity maps and reverses composites on rings; applying $\Spec$ reverses them again and gives $u$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-profinite-to-proetale-finite-limits] to this $u$ to obtain preservation of finite limits. Apply [lem-sfb-profinite-to-proetale-cover-preserving] to a finite jointly surjective family of profinite sets to obtain a covering family on $(\Spec\Z)_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Finally [lem-sfb-profinite-to-proetale-continuous] says exactly that restriction of any sheaf along $u$ is a sheaf, giving the asserted continuity.

source.place: part 1; first paragraph of the blueprint proof

proof.text: For X take profiniteToProEtOf X, the composite of u with base change along its structure map, as in [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects] and [def-sfb-finite-lower-star]. Apply the cofiltered finite-quotient clause of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor] to Profinite.asLimitCone S: Profinite.asLimit proves it limiting and each quotient projection is surjective. Forgetting from Over X preserves this connected limit, giving the asserted scheme limit. For finite coproducts, the composite functor to schemes is continuous into the subcanonical pro-etale scheme site, by continuity of u and base change. Restriction of each representable is therefore a sheaf, hence a sheaf for the extensive topology on Profinite. Its finite-product condition and Yoneda give preservation of finite coproducts (the proved coproducts_of_continuous helper of the test-object module). Finite-limit preservation of the relative test functor sends the singleton to the terminal object over X; its structural morphism to X is consequently an isomorphism. At Spec Z the natural comparison in the final clause of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor] transports the limit and coproduct properties to profiniteToScheme. Its singleton structural map is an isomorphism because profiniteToScheme preserves the terminal object: forget from Over Spec Z is an equivalence since Spec Z is terminal.

source.place: part 2; second paragraph of the blueprint proof, also the inverse-limit formula of part 1

proof.text: Take restriction along $u$ for $p_*$, exactly as in [def-sfb-point-lower-star]. The left Kan extension of every underlying abelian presheaf exists by [lem-sfb-point-lan-exists]. Thus [def-sfb-point-upper-star] defines $p^*$ as this left Kan extension followed by sheafification. The natural bijection $\Hom(p^*F,G)\cong\Hom(F,p_*G)$ is precisely the adjunction stated in [def-sfb-point-adjunction]. These are sheaves of abelian groups throughout, using the size convention of the small pro-étale sites, with the coefficient universe enlarged accordingly.

source.place: part 3; third paragraph of the blueprint proof, construction and adjunction

proof.text: For the sheafified tensor product over $\Z$, [lem-sfb-point-upper-star-unit] gives the lax monoidal structure on $p_*$, its adjoint oplax structure on $p^*$, and invertibility of $p^*\underline\Z\to\underline\Z$. By [lem-sfb-point-upper-star-tensor], the tensor comparisons $p^*(F\otimes G)\to p^*F\otimes p^*G$ are also invertible. Their inverses give the strong monoidal structure. To check coherence, write $P=p^*$, $\delta_{F,G}\colon P(F\otimes G)\to PF\otimes PG$ and $\epsilon\colon P\mathbf1\to\mathbf1$. With the canonical associators inserted, oplax associativity equates $(\delta_{F,G}\otimes1)\circ\delta_{F\otimes G,H}$ and $(1\otimes\delta_{G,H})\circ\delta_{F,G\otimes H}$; taking inverses gives the monoidal associativity identity for $\delta^{-1}$. The left and right unit identities follow by inverting the oplax unit identities, with unit map $\epsilon^{-1}$. The symmetry compatibility is the assertion of [lem-sfb-point-upper-star-braided]. Hence $p^*$ is strong monoidal and braided for the tensor product specified in the statement.

source.place: part 3; third paragraph of the blueprint proof, monoidal and braided structure

proof.text: Define $p_X^*=\pi_X^*\circ p^*$ by [def-sfb-upper-star-from-point], using the pullback of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star] at $g=\pi_X$ and $\mathcal A=\Ab$. This $\pi_X^*$ is strong monoidal by [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal] and symmetric by [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-braided]. Together with [lem-sfb-point-upper-star-braided], its composite tensor comparison is the pair of isomorphisms $\pi_X^*p^*(F\otimes G)\to\pi_X^*(p^*F\otimes p^*G)\to\pi_X^*p^*F\otimes\pi_X^*p^*G$, and its unit comparison is $\pi_X^*p^*\underline\Z\to\pi_X^*\underline\Z\to\underline\Z$. Write $P=p^*$ and $Q=\pi_X^*$. Both ways of expanding a triple tensor first expand inside $Q$ using the comparisons of $P$, then expand $Q$ using its comparisons. Naturality of the comparison of $Q$ allows these two expansions to be put in that order; associativity for $P$ identifies the first expansions, and associativity for $Q$ identifies the second ones, with their canonical associators. For either unit diagram, naturality first moves the unit comparison of $P$ inside $Q$; the unit identity for $P$ followed by the unit identity for $Q$ reduces the composite to the required unitor. More explicitly, symmetry follows from $\beta_{QPF,QPG}\circ\delta^Q_{PF,PG}\circ Q(\delta^P_{F,G})=\delta^Q_{PG,PF}\circ Q(\beta_{PF,PG})\circ Q(\delta^P_{F,G})=\delta^Q_{PG,PF}\circ Q(\delta^P_{G,F})\circ QP(\beta_{F,G})$, using the symmetry identity for $Q$ and then for $P$. Thus $p_X^*$ is strong monoidal and braided.

source.place: part 4; final paragraph of the blueprint proof, definition and monoidal structure

proof.text:
For a condensed abelian group $F$ and an abelian sheaf $G$ on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$, [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction] at $g=\pi_X$ and [def-sfb-point-adjunction] give, naturally in both variables,
$$\Hom(\pi_X^*p^*F,G)\cong\Hom(p^*F,\pi_{X*}G)\cong\Hom(F,p_*\pi_{X*}G).$$
Using the definition [def-sfb-upper-star-from-point], this exhibits $p_X^*$ as left adjoint to $p_*\circ\pi_{X*}$, with no properness or finiteness condition on $X$ or on its structure map.

source.place: part 4; final paragraph of the blueprint proof, composite adjunction

proof.text:
By [def-sfb-point-lower-star] and [def-sfb-finite-lower-star] at $g=\pi_X$, the right adjoint just obtained evaluates as
$$(p_*\pi_{X*}G)(S)=(\pi_{X*}G)(\Spec LC(S,\Z))=G(\Spec LC(S,\Z)\times_{\Spec\Z}X)=G(X[S]),$$
where the last equality is [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects]. This calculation also respects a map $g\colon S'\to S$: both restriction maps are $G$ applied contravariantly to the base change of the morphism induced by $h\mapsto h\circ g$. For a morphism $\eta\colon G\to H$ of sheaves, both constructions act by its component $\eta_{X[S]}$, so the identification is natural in $G$ as well. Thus this calculation gives a canonical natural isomorphism of restriction functors, with the fiber products identified by their canonical isomorphisms. Its values are sheaves because it is the composite of the two sheaf-valued direct images. Consequently the adjunction of the previous step identifies $p_X^*$ as inverse image along $u_X$.

source.place: part 4; final paragraph of the blueprint proof, section calculation and its naturality
